key_insight: Supersonic turbulent shear layers become self-similar far downstream, and their growth, asymmetry, and entrainment can be collapsed with compressibility-aware scalings that account for convective Mach number and velocity parameter effects.
engineering_relevance: These results provide usable scaling laws and entrainment predictions for high-speed mixing layers, which are important for propulsion, combustion, and other compressible-flow system designs.
method: Direct Numerical Simulations of spatially developing supersonic turbulent shear layers.
Parametric study over multiple convective Mach numbers (Mc) and velocity parameters (λ).
Derivation of self-similar forms of continuity, momentum, and energy equations plus an approximate cross-stream velocity equation.
evidence_signal: DNS results show collapse of normalized velocity and turbulence profiles in the self-similar region, constant normalized Reynolds-stress peaks, and linear growth of shear-layer and momentum thickness.
watch_item: The proposed scalings and closed-form entrainment relation are validated within DNS cases studied here, so extrapolation to different geometries, Reynolds numbers, or strongly non-equilibrium flows should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Numerical Study of Compressibility and Velocity Parameter Effects on Spatially Evolving Supersonic Turbulent Shear Layers
